question: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of a concave mirror with a focal length of 20 cm. Its image will be formed at a distance of □( ), and will be □( ).
solution:
The correct answer is __**60 cm, Actual**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of a concave mirror.
 
• The focal length of the concave mirror is 20 cm.
 
• The image formed will be real and inverted as it is formed on the same side of the mirror as the object.
 
• Using the mirror formula, the image distance can be calculated to be 60 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mirror Formula**

 
 
• The mirror formula relates the object distance (u), the image distance (v), and the focal length (f) of a spherical mirror.
 
• The formula is given by:

 **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**
 
• In this case, the object distance (u) is -30 cm (negative because the object is placed in front of the mirror).
 
• The focal length (f) is -20 cm (negative for concave mirrors).
 
• By substituting these values into the mirror formula, we get:
 
 
• 1/(-20) = 1/v + 1/(-30)
 
• Simplifying, we get: 1/v = 1/(-20) - 1/(-30)
 
• 1/v = -1/20 + 1/30
 
• 1/v = (-3 + 2) / 60
 
• 1/v = -1/60
 
• v = -60 cm
 
 
 
• The negative sign indicates that the image is formed on the same side as the object, confirming the image is real and inverted.
 
 
 
• **Concave Mirror**
 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that curves inward like a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• Concave mirrors can form real and virtual images depending on the position of the object.
 
• They are used in applications requiring the convergence of light, such as in telescopes, headlights of vehicles, and shaving mirrors.
